name: When should I consider repairing versus replacing my commercial water heater?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider repairing versus replacing my commercial water heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding between repair and replacement for a commercial water heater often depends on its age, the extent of the damage, and the frequency of past repairs. If a water heater is old (typically past its warranty or expected lifespan of 8-12 years) or requires frequent, costly repairs, replacement might be more economical long-term. Conversely, newer units with minor, isolated issues are usually better candidates for repair. CG Plumbing Solutions can help assess your unit's condition and provide a recommendation based on its efficiency and remaining lifespan.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider repair for newer units with minor issues, but replacement might be better for old water heaters or those needing frequent, costly repairs.
